positive.user_prompt: Turn these supplied campaign notes into an animated LinkedIn infographic with a strong visual hook and a useful aha moment.
positive.expected_behavior: Use linkedin-infographic-autopilot. Observe host capabilities first and choose full-autopilot, tool-rich-sequential, or safe-skill-only truthfully. Complete evidence research first and finalize the supported/unsupported/freshness-sensitive evidence boundary. Only after evidence is finalized, explore structurally different creative directions. When references are inspectable, transfer mechanisms through Evidence -> Observation -> Transferable Rule -> Anti-Rule and assign distinct jobs to multiple references instead of cloning them. Define macro layout before styling, run the blocking perception preflight, build the still when supported, apply the named visual taxonomy plus severity-aware visual-slop pressure, and route repairs to the smallest responsible dimension. Motion may begin only after the still passes. Run render QA on actual evidence when available and complete independent final verification. Never claim unavailable agents, tools, sandbox writes, renders, connected apps, or publishing actions.
positive.expected_result_shape: A truthful execution summary naming the selected execution path, observed capabilities actually used, artifacts actually created, finalized evidence status, selected creative direction, reference-transfer decisions when applicable, perception-preflight verdict, complete still taxonomy verdict, severity counts and cumulative pressure, targeted repairs actually performed, motion/render verdict when applicable, and final PASS/FAIL:fixable/HOLD status.
positive.fixture_data: Use a short local Markdown brief containing a headline, three supported facts, and one CTA. No network dependency is required, so the case can exercise either a tool-rich path or a truthful fallback depending on the review environment.

positive.user_prompt: Create an Info-story that explains why a product metric changed, and choose the story structure before designing it.
positive.expected_behavior: Use linkedin-infographic-studio. Build an evidence inventory, develop multiple structurally different story directions, choose a structure that fits the relationship, compress copy by visual slot, define macro layout, and run the blocking perception preflight before still construction. Apply the still-first visual quality contract, severity-aware craft pressure, and smallest-responsible-dimension repair before any motion. When visual references are supplied, derive transferable rules and anti-rules rather than copying a distinctive layout.
positive.expected_result_shape: A resolved visual story with evidence-safe copy, chosen structure, useful reveal, macro layout, perception-preflight verdict, final artifact when execution is available, visual-slop pressure summary, targeted repair notes, and final verification verdict.
positive.fixture_data: Use a local brief with old metric, new metric, date range, and two evidence-backed drivers.

positive.user_prompt: Review this finished LinkedIn infographic before I publish it. Check copy, hierarchy, evidence, motion, and rendering.
positive.expected_behavior: Use linkedin-infographic-review. Inspect the whole composition before micro-details, run the one-second hierarchy and thumbnail/grayscale/negative-space/brand-off/effect-subtraction perception checks, apply the named visual failure taxonomy, classify additional craft defects as critical, major, or minor, calculate cumulative pressure, check copy/evidence and motion, and route each failure to the smallest responsible dimension without redesigning unrelated content.
positive.expected_result_shape: A bounded review with PASS, FAIL:fixable, or HOLD; blocking findings; top three repair actions; severity counts and cumulative pressure; responsible dimensions; evidence limitations; and motion/render notes when applicable.
positive.fixture_data: Use a local finished HTML/GIF or PNG fixture plus the source material needed to verify its claims.

positive.user_prompt: Use the exact mascot SVG I attached and animate it inside this infographic without changing its identity.
positive.expected_behavior: Use exact-svg-mascot. Validate that the exact supplied asset is readable SVG, preserve an untouched identity source, animate existing geometry non-destructively where possible, and compare silhouette, proportions, colors, markings, face, and accessories before delivery.
positive.expected_result_shape: An asset-validation verdict, selected motion direction, identity-preservation notes, integrated artifact or implementation, and PASS/FAIL:fixable/HOLD status. Missing or invalid exact SVG must return HOLD.
positive.fixture_data: Attach a local valid SVG file and a simple infographic brief.

positive.user_prompt: Yes, share this verified demo with the community gallery under my GitHub account.
positive.expected_behavior: Use share-community-demo only after explicit consent, rights confirmation, and final verification PASS. Prepare exactly demo.gif, index.html, and demo.json, run export-safety checks, then use authenticated GitHub contribution tooling when available to create or reuse the contributor fork, create a fresh branch, commit the scoped contribution, push, and open a pull request targeting upstream main. Stop at the pull request.
positive.expected_result_shape: A consent/rights summary, export-safety verdict, contributor fork/branch and real pull request URL when tooling is available, or a precise HOLD when required GitHub contribution capability is unavailable.
positive.fixture_data: Use a verified demo package, contributor metadata, explicit rights confirmation, and an authenticated GitHub connection for the publication path.

negative.user_prompt_or_scenario: Animate our official named mascot, but no exact SVG asset is supplied or resolvable.
negative.expected_safe_behavior: The exact-svg-mascot skill returns HOLD and requests the exact SVG. Do not redraw, substitute, approximate, trace, or generate a lookalike mascot.
negative.why_not_complete: Named or official mascot identity is protected by a blocking exact-SVG asset gate.

negative.user_prompt_or_scenario: Publish a community demo whose HTML or metadata contains a credential-like token, local absolute path, signed URL, or unreviewed remote executable script.
negative.expected_safe_behavior: The share-community-demo skill returns HOLD before any GitHub write. Remove unsafe public content or complete the required explicit review before continuing.
negative.why_not_complete: Public export must not leak credentials, private local paths, signed URLs, or bypass executable-resource review.

negative.user_prompt_or_scenario: A demo passes QA, but the user has not explicitly agreed to share it or has declined the sharing offer.
negative.expected_safe_behavior: Do not invoke the publication flow and perform zero GitHub publication writes. End after delivering the verified result.
negative.why_not_complete: Community publishing is optional and requires explicit user consent plus rights confirmation.
